title: Build and Deploy Docker Image with GitHub Actions
description: Create a CD pipeline that builds a Docker image and pushes it to GitHub Container Registry
objective: Students will create a GitHub Actions CD workflow that automatically builds a Docker image from their FastAPI app, pushes it to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR), and verifies the deployment pipeline works end-to-end

steps.title: Prepare the Project with Dockerfile
steps.instructions:
We will use the FastAPI project from the CI lab. Make sure your project has these files:

**Project structure:**
```
techpath-student-api/
  .github/workflows/ci.yml    (from Lab 14-A)
  app/
    __init__.py
    main.py
  Dockerfile
  requirements.txt
  tests/
    test_main.py
```

**Create `Dockerfile`** in the project root:
```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim

LABEL maintainer="TechPath Institute"
LABEL description="TechPath Student API"

ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

EXPOSE 8000

CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

**Create `.dockerignore`:**
```
.git
.github
__pycache__
*.pyc
.env
.venv
tests/
*.md
```

**Test locally:**
```bash
docker build -t techpath-api .
docker run -d -p 8000:8000 techpath-api
curl http://localhost:8000/health
```

Verify the Docker build works locally before setting up the CD pipeline.

steps.title: Create the CD Workflow File
steps.instructions:
Create `.github/workflows/cd.yml` — the deployment pipeline:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/cd.yml
# TechPath Institute — CD Pipeline
# Builds Docker image and pushes to GitHub Container Registry

name: CD - Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:  # Allow manual trigger from GitHub UI

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    name: Build and Push Docker Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Extract metadata (tags, labels)
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
          tags: |
            type=sha,prefix=
            type=raw,value=latest

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}

      - name: Print image URL
        run: |
          echo "Image pushed successfully!"
          echo "Pull with: docker pull ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest"
```

This workflow:
1. Triggers when code is pushed to `main` branch
2. Logs into GitHub Container Registry using the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`
3. Builds the Docker image from our Dockerfile
4. Tags it with the commit SHA and `latest`
5. Pushes it to GHCR

**Note:** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is automatically provided — no need to create a secret for it!

steps.title: Configure Repository Permissions
steps.instructions:
Before pushing, configure your GitHub repository for GHCR access.

**1. Go to your GitHub repository** in the browser.

**2. Check Actions permissions:**
- Go to Settings > Actions > General
- Under "Workflow permissions", select **Read and write permissions**
- Check "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"
- Click Save

**3. Commit and push all files:**
```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Add CD pipeline and Dockerfile for TechPath API"
git push origin main
```

**4. Watch the CD workflow run:**
- Go to your repository on GitHub
- Click the **Actions** tab
- You should see "CD - Build & Push Docker Image" running
- Click on it to watch the progress in real time

**5. Check each step:**
- Checkout code — downloads your code
- Log in to GHCR — authenticates with the registry
- Extract metadata — generates image tags
- Build and push — builds Docker image and uploads it

The workflow should complete with a green checkmark. If it fails, click on the failed step to see the error message.

**Screenshot:** Take a screenshot of the successful workflow run in the Actions tab.

steps.title: Verify the Published Image
steps.instructions:
After the CD pipeline runs successfully, verify your Docker image was published to GHCR.

**1. Find your image on GitHub:**
- Go to your GitHub profile
- Click on **Packages** tab (or visit github.com/YOUR_USERNAME?tab=packages)
- You should see your image listed
- Click on it to see details — tags, size, pull command

**2. Pull and run the image from GHCR:**
```bash
# Login to GHCR (use a Personal Access Token)
echo YOUR_TOKEN | docker login ghcr.io -u YOUR_USERNAME --password-stdin

# Pull the image
docker pull ghcr.io/YOUR_USERNAME/techpath-student-api:latest

# Run it
docker run -d -p 8000:8000 --name api-from-ghcr ghcr.io/YOUR_USERNAME/techpath-student-api:latest

# Test it
curl http://localhost:8000/health
```

**3. Verify the image details:**
```bash
docker images | grep techpath
```

You should see the image pulled from GHCR with the correct tag and size.

**4. Make a code change and verify CD runs again:**
- Edit `app/main.py` — change the version string to `2.0`
- Commit and push to main
- Watch the CD pipeline automatically build and push a new image

**Screenshot:** Take a screenshot of the Packages page showing your published Docker image.

steps.title: Add CI Gate Before CD
steps.instructions:
Best practice: CD should only run after CI passes. Let us connect the two workflows.

**Update `.github/workflows/cd.yml`** to run only after CI succeeds:

```yaml
name: CD - Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI - Test & Lint"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    name: Build and Push Docker Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Only run if CI succeeded
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}

    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Extract metadata
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
          tags: |
            type=sha,prefix=
            type=raw,value=latest

      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
```

Now the flow is:
1. Push to main triggers CI (test + lint)
2. If CI passes, CD automatically starts (build + push Docker image)
3. If CI fails, CD does not run — broken code never gets deployed

**Commit and test:**
```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Connect CI and CD pipelines - deploy only after tests pass"
git push origin main
```

Watch both workflows in the Actions tab — CI runs first, then CD.

**Submit:**
1. Both workflow files: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/cd.yml`
2. Your `Dockerfile` and `.dockerignore`
3. Screenshot of Actions tab showing CI and CD workflows
4. Screenshot of Packages page showing your Docker image on GHCR
5. Screenshot of the running container pulled from GHCR
